chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said:

In Medina, there was a foolish man who would make people laugh at him. He said: This man has exhausted me in trying to make him laugh -- meaning Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). He said: So Ali (peace be upon him) passed by, and behind him were two of his servants. The man came and snatched his cloak from his neck, then went away. Ali (peace be upon him) did not turn toward him. So they followed the man and took the cloak back from him. They brought it to him and placed it on him.
He said to them: Who is this? They said: This is a foolish man whom the people of Medina laugh at. He said: Say to him: Indeed, God has a Day in which the invalidators will lose.

key_terms.المبطلون: Al-Mubtilun - those who deal in falsehood and vanity; the invalidators
key_terms.بطال: Battal - idle, foolish person; one who engages in vain behavior

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Zayn al-Abidin respond to the man who snatched his cloak?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq narrates the forbearance of Imam Zayn al-Abidin (Ali ibn al-Husayn). A jester in Medina, who amused people with his antics, snatched the Imam's cloak as a prank. The Imam did not even turn around, and when told who did it, he simply warned that God has a Day of Judgment when those who deal in falsehood will lose. This illustrates the Imam's legendary patience and his refusal to be provoked by worldly foolishness.
